name: Amangiri
positioning: Aman's desert resort in Canyon Point, Utah, blending sharp-angled concrete architecture with the rugged landscape
best_for: Travelers who want a remote, quiet desert escape with dark night skies
Families who want a resort with games, pool toys and babysitting

facts.text: The rooms are a contemporary interpretation of Native American shelters.
The terrace of the room described by Condé Nast Traveler has an outdoor fireplace.
Guests can explore slot canyons with a local Navajo guide.
Educational stargazing sessions are organized in collaboration with a local observatory.
Amangiri is family-friendly, with books, games and pool toys available on request and a babysitting service.
Much of the main hotel is accessible for wheelchair users, with ramps for the entrance and front desk, restaurant, pool, and spa and fitness center.
The resort lists Page Municipal Airport (PGA) as a flight arrival option.
Condé Nast Traveler lists Amangiri on its Gold List, including 2026.

highlights.text: The architecture blends modern, sharp-angled concrete with the rugged desert landscape.
Camp Sarika, a short walk from the main property, has tented pavilions next to the cliffs, each with its own plunge pool and a golf buggy.
The resort follows International Dark-Sky Association guidelines so that all property lighting minimizes light pollution.
Each spa treatment begins with a white sage burning ritual, a local practice intended to cleanse and heal.
The cuisine mixes Mexican and Native American influences, using ingredients such as blue corn, green chilli and prickly pear.

considerations.text: From Phoenix Sky Harbor or Las Vegas Harry Reid airports, the resort lists an approximately 4.5 hour scenic drive to reach Amangiri.
Most meals are eaten at the resort, which is all-inclusive.
WhataHotel notes the remote desert location requires significant travel planning.
